newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean steel output seen up 8.0 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean steel output seen up 8.0 pct in 1996.

text.p: South Korea's total crude steel production is forecast to rise eight percent this year over 1995 to reach 39.7 million tonnes, Sung-Woo Kim, a senior manager at the Korea Iron & Steel Association said on Tuesday.

Kim said the growth in output stemmed from a 9.3 percent increase in the country's overall steel production capacity to 42.2 million tonnes over the same period with the installation of new electric arc furnaces by POSCO (2.2 million tonnes), Kangwon Industries (1.0 million), Kia Steel (0.2 million) and Korea Iron and Steel (0.1 million).
He was speaking at Metal Bulletin's 4th Asian Steel Conference being held in Seoul.

South Korea has increased its steelmaking capacity in response to growing domestic demand for steel despite a slight weakening in annualised GDP growth to 7.6 percent during the first half of 1996 compared with an 8.6 percent rise for the whole of 1995.

During the first seven months of 1996 national car production rose 12 percent. There were also increases in shipbuilding (78.2 pct), deliveries of industrial machinery (17.2 pct) and the value of construction contracts (18.8 pct).

Kim said that from the second-half of this year, growth rates in the major steel-consuming sectors began a gradual fall, which could be regarded as an early indication of a slowdown in steel demand growth.
